name: CaptionMate
oneLine: US phone-call caption app with AI captions in 100+ languages, free through the FCC for eligible people with hearing loss; owned by InnoCaption's company since 2024.

platforms.detail: On the App Store for iPhone and iPad (also listed for Apple Vision) and on Google Play for phones and tablets. One account can be signed in on several devices. The CaptionMate web app was retired; the company points computer users to InnoCaption Web.

deviceRequirements.text: iOS 15.0 or later; Android not stated
deviceRequirements.detail: The App Store lists iOS 15.0 or later for iPhone and iPadOS 15.0 or later for iPad. No CaptionMate page gives a minimum Android version.

roomCaptions.detail: CaptionMate says it can't be used when both people are in the same room. It is paid for by a federal relay fund, and using it instead of an in-person captioner is against the law.

groupConversations.detail: It can be used on conference calls and to dial into online meetings and webinars. It can't be used for a group in the same room.

languages.detail: You pick the languages you want and can switch during a call. The app's menus come in English, Spanish, Vietnamese and Chinese. The About page says 150+ languages; the home page uses 150+ for the app's menus.

offline.detail: Calls connect over Wi-Fi or mobile data, so the app needs an internet connection.

speakerLabels.detail: It captions what you say and what the other person says, so you can read the whole call. Nothing is described for groups in the room.

translation.detail: Captions match the language spoken on the call. CaptionMate says it can't translate speech from one language to another.

saveTranscripts.detail: Each call's transcript is saved on the device used for the call. Transcripts aren't stored on CaptionMate's servers or synced to your other devices, and deleting the app deletes them.

export.text: Share by email or another app
export.detail: You can send a transcript through any app on your phone, such as email, to keep a copy. The About page says you can share a call transcript with the other person.

fileUpload.detail: No CaptionMate page mentions transcribing audio or video files.

summaries.detail: No CaptionMate page mentions AI summaries of calls.

customWords.detail: You can add names and words you use often that the AI may have trouble captioning.

display.detail: You can change the font size and colour of the captions.

soundAlerts.detail: No alerts for sounds around you are described.

phoneCalls.detail: Captions both sides of incoming and outgoing calls on your own number through call forwarding, and voicemail as text (no audio). You can call numbers outside the US. The privacy policy describes how 911 calls are handled. Text messages aren't covered.

videoCalls.detail: You can dial into a video conference or online meeting by phone. The app can't caption FaceTime calls; the company points to its sister app, InnoCaption Video.

mediaOnDevice.detail: No CaptionMate page describes captioning videos or other media playing on the device.

humanCaptioners.detail: CaptionMate says its captions are 100% AI and it does not use human stenographers. InnoCaption, from the same company, also offers live stenographers.

privacy.text: Cloud; call audio not kept after the call
privacy.detail: Call audio is sent to servers in the US, some run by third parties, and discarded when the call ends. CaptionMate says no call audio is logged for machine learning and only you can read your transcripts.

account.text: Yes; name, DOB, last 4 of SSN
account.detail: Registration asks for your full name, date of birth, last four digits of your SSN, home address and cell number, for the FCC's relay fund. No doctor's or audiologist's statement is needed.

availability.detail: Only for eligible users based in the US or a US territory such as Puerto Rico or Guam, with a US cell number, home address and SSN. The app was not found in the UK, Canada or Mexico App Stores.

freePlan.detail: Free for eligible people who are deaf or hard of hearing and need captions on phone calls, paid from the FCC's relay fund. Your phone plan's data and call charges still apply.

price.detail: Free on the App Store with no in-app purchases (US App Store, October 2026).

accessibilityFunding.detail: The FCC lists Mezmo Corporation (dba CaptionMate) with full certification for IP captioned telephone service. The service is paid from the federal TRS Fund.

strengths.text: Free for eligible users in the US, paid for by the FCC's relay fund.
Captions both sides of phone calls in more than 100 languages, and you can switch language during a call.
Works with your existing phone number and turns voicemail into text.
Streams calls to Bluetooth hearing aids and cochlear implants.

limits.text: It can't be used for in-person conversations; CaptionMate says this is against the law for its FCC-funded service.
Only for eligible users in the US and US territories with a US cell number, home address and SSN.
Captions are AI only, with no human stenographers, and nothing is translated.
Transcripts stay on one device and are deleted with the app unless you share them first.

quotes: CaptionMate is a mobile app that uses automated speech recognition technology to instantly transcribe both sides of a phone call, so that the entire conversation can be read in real time.
Over 100 languages

quotes: CaptionMate is able to provide captioning in more than 100 languages.

sources.title: Call confidentiality
quotes: All calls are fully captioned by automated speech recognition software. Our service does not use human stenographers for captioning.
The ASR (automatic speech recognition) engine does not store or otherwise keep any record of your speech, transcription or conversation after the call has ended.

sources.title: Personal information required for registration
quotes: The personal information we are required to provide to the FCC’s Telecommunications Relay Services (TRS) Fund Administrator for compliance purposes include: full name, date of birth, last four digits of your social security number, residential address and cell phone number.

sources.title: View and delete call transcripts
quotes: CaptionMate automatically saves the transcript of each call. Call transcripts will only be available on the device you used for the call.
your call transcripts are not saved on CaptionMate servers.

sources.title: Share and Save Call Transcripts
quotes: Select the app you'd like to use to send the transcript. An easy way to save them is to use an email app to send them to your own email address.

sources.title: In-person Captioning
quotes: CaptionMate cannot be used for in-person captioning- or, in other words- when both parties are in the same room together.
It is against the law to use the service as a substitute for hiring an in-person captioner to provide access.
For example, this could include phone calls to family and friends; work calls; conference calls; online meetings; and even webinars. Again, this would not apply to when people are in the same room.

sources.title: CaptionMate eligibility and why it's free
quotes: CaptionMate's service is offered free of charge to eligible individuals who are deaf or hard of hearing and need captions to understand phone conversations.
Our service is funded and administered by the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) through the Telecommunications Relay Service (TRS) fund and is available to eligible users in the United States.
Individuals living in US territories including Puerto Rico, Guam, the US Virgin Islands, American Samoa, Northern Mariana Islands, and US Minor Outlying Islands are also eligible to use the app.
No signed statement from a doctor or audiologist is required to use our service

sources.title: CaptionMate Joins the InnoCaption Family
quotes: InnoCaption, a leading mobile call captioning technology provider for the deaf and hard of hearing community, announced today that it has completed the acquisition of CaptionMate.

CaptionMate uses advanced automated speech recognition technology to provide real-time captions of phone calls for users in more than 100 languages and offers unique features like the ability to change the mobile app interface language to Spanish, Chinese or Vietnamese.
With the closing of this acquisition, CaptionMate will be supported by the InnoCaption team as a standalone service.

notes: Owner: InnoCaption completed the acquisition of CaptionMate on November 1, 2024 (CaptionMate news page, copied from InnoCaption's own release). The App Store seller and Google Play developer are Mezmo Corporation (Play contact info@innocaption.com, Irvine CA), and the FCC lists 'CaptionMate, LLC' with full IP CTS certification under Mezmo Corporation (dba CaptionMate). The privacy policy and terms still name CaptionMate LLC (Hixson, TN), and the App Store copyright line is Clarity Products LLC. How it differs from InnoCaption, from official pages: CaptionMate stays a standalone service supported by the InnoCaption team; its captions are 100% AI with no human stenographers, while InnoCaption also offers live stenographers; CaptionMate captions in 100+ languages (InnoCaption's help centre lists 20+ secondary AI languages); the acquisition release calls the Spanish, Chinese and Vietnamese app interface a unique CaptionMate feature; the CaptionMate web app was retired and points to InnoCaption Web; CaptionMate's help pages describe no transcript backup or AI summaries, which InnoCaption has (not stated, not 'no'). No page compares the two apps directly. Language conflicts: home page, App Store, Google Play and help centre say 100+ caption languages; the About page says '150+ languages available', and the home page uses 150+ for the app interface, while the help centre says the interface has four languages (English, Spanish, Vietnamese, Chinese Simplified) and the App Store lists five (adds Traditional Chinese). Not found: minimum Android version (not in the Play page's HTML or the help centre), any usage limit, file transcription, summaries, sound alerts, sign language. The App Store privacy label lists Identifiers as data used to track you (not used on the page). Pages were read with curl (full HTML); the Google Play page through its static HTML. The App Store lookup API returned no result for the UK, Canada and Mexico storefronts; other countries were not checked. A web search for InnoCaption help articles about CaptionMate could not be run (search limit); the InnoCaption help centre was not searched for CaptionMate.
